summary: Imported SPEAR worlds are self-contained at the Unreal source-content directory level only when the whole per-world Content/SPEAR/Scenes/<world> folder is kept together. A .umap alone is not self-contained because it references mesh assets under the sibling Meshes directory. Cooked runnable output is currently a monolithic Standalone-Development Linux archive with one SpearSim-Linux.pak, so a single cooked world is not cleanly separable unless a dedicated per-world/DLC PAK workflow is added. Infinigen output folders are regeneration/reimport sources, not SPEAR runtime assets.

findings.message: For source-level sharing with another SPEAR developer, archive the whole Unreal content folder for each world, preserving its relative path: cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Content/SPEAR/Scenes/one_bed_apartment, cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Content/SPEAR/Scenes/college_classroom, or cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Content/SPEAR/Scenes/infinigen_indoors_0000. Do not share only Maps/*.umap; the maps depend on sibling Meshes/*.uasset files.

Recommended source-content archive grouping: one archive per world folder under Content/SPEAR/Scenes, restored to the same relative path in a compatible SpearSim Unreal project and UE/SPEAR version. Current imported worlds do not have Materials or Textures subdirectories because material and texture import was disabled.

For a runnable simulator, archive cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Standalone-Development/Linux as the shareable build output. That directory includes SpearSim.sh, binaries, Engine runtime dependencies, and SpearSim/Content/Paks/SpearSim-Linux.pak. The Saved/StagedBuilds/Linux/SpearSim tree is a staging copy/intermediate, not the preferred handoff path.

A single cooked world cannot currently be archived as a clean standalone runnable artifact from the observed output. The current cook/package flow produced one monolithic SpearSim-Linux.pak containing the cooked project payload. The Saved/Cooked per-world .uasset/.uexp/.ubulk files are not enough by themselves for a runnable sim and should not be treated as a portable single-world package.

For one_bed_apartment regeneration/reimport, archive /home/yashturkar/Workspace/infinigen/outputs/one_bed_apartment_spear_light plus provenance from /home/yashturkar/Workspace/infinigen/outputs/one_bed_apartment/one_bed_floorplan.json and optionally run_generate_one_bed.sh. Key artifacts include coarse/scene.blend, coarse/polycounts.txt, spear_export_r256/export_scene.blend/export_scene.fbx, spear_export_r256/export_logs.log, and logs/*.log.

For college_classroom regeneration/reimport, archive /home/yashturkar/Workspace/infinigen/outputs/college_classroom. Key artifacts include coarse/scene.blend, scripts/create_college_classroom.py, spear_export_r256/export_scene.blend/export_scene.fbx, spear_export_r256/export_logs.log, logs/*.log, preview, and status_college_classroom_20260630T145523Z.txt.

Infinigen folders are not SPEAR runtime assets. SPEAR loads the imported Unreal .umap/.uasset content or cooked PAK output; Infinigen .blend, FBX, scripts, floorplans, and logs are for re-exporting/reimporting or auditing provenance.

Both one_bed_apartment and college_classroom were imported with --no-auto-generate-collision --no-import-materials --no-import-textures. Expect limited/default visual material fidelity and likely missing generated collision unless later repaired; inspect visual quality, scale, lighting, collision/navigation behavior, and PlayerStart usability before data collection.

follow_up_recommendations: Add a short docs section that formalizes three archive bundles: Unreal source content, full standalone runnable build, and Infinigen regeneration bundle.
If single-world cooked sharing is required, define and validate a dedicated per-world PAK or DLC-style packaging workflow instead of relying on the current monolithic SpearSim-Linux.pak.
Before archiving for external use, run a small restore test in a clean compatible SPEAR checkout: copy the per-world Content/SPEAR/Scenes folder, open/cook the map, and launch with --map-path.
